name: Ortur Laser Master 3 20W
tagline: Community-favorite open-frame diode: best LM3 value
tldr: The 20W LM3 is the configuration most buyers mean when they say 'Laser Master 3'. Strong engraving, light cutting, huge community: verify you are not accidentally ordering the 10W SKU.

engraveExample.description: Filled photo or logo on birch plywood

cutExample.description: Simple square cut-out from 3 mm basswood

pros: Free Air Pump 1.0 in Ortur's basic set (October 2026)
Square 0.08 × 0.08 mm spot, which Ortur says gives 256 grey levels
Fills at ~70–150 mm/s: a 10 × 10 cm photo in ~10–15 min

editorialDepth.advantages: Ortur Laser Master 3 20W is the versatile hobby / side-business SKU: clean engraving and light wood or leather cuts with comparable benchmarks on Maker Atlas.
editorialDepth.limitations: Open-frame: glasses and exhaust required. Not a CO₂ replacement for clear acrylic or heavy thick-stock production.

cons: Working area shrinks to 400 × 380 mm (400 × 355 mm with the Z-height adjuster)
$639.99 basic set: more than double the entry LM3
Long cutting runs fill the room with smoke unless the exhaust is ducted outside
beginnerNotes: This profile is the 20W SKU on Ortur Laser Master 3. Read the TL;DR and benchmarks above, then compare other power options via the chips before buying.
proTips: Use air assist for cuts, lower scan speed for photo engraving. Multiple passes at moderate speed beat one aggressive pass. Check the flagship tier’s cut benchmark if you quote production times to customers.

accessories.note: 450 nm diode: verify OD with seller

mainObjective: Everyday engraving plus reliable light cutting on wood, leather, and dark acrylic

faq.question: What does Ortur claim the LM3 20W cuts in one pass?
faq.answer: Ortur's page shows one-pass demo cuts in 15 mm pine, 10 mm plywood and 8 mm black acrylic. Those are demos, not guaranteed maxima. In our benchmarks a 10 × 10 cm square in 3 mm basswood takes about 5–8 min at 3–10 mm/s, and around 8 mm basswood is a realistic everyday limit.

faq.question: Which LM3 20W set should I buy?
faq.answer: In October 2026 Ortur listed the 20W Basic set at $639.99 (with a free Air Pump 1.0), the Pro set at $719.98, the Rotary set at $839.97, the Extended set at $929.96 and the All-in-1 set at $1,399.99. The Extended set raises the working length to about 850 mm according to Ortur.

faq.question: Is the 20W worth twice the price of the LM3 10W?
faq.answer: If you cut, yes: for about $340 more it cuts our 3 mm square in about a third less time (5–8 min against 8–12 min) and fills at ~70–150 mm/s instead of 20–42 mm/s. Ortur also advertises colour marking on stainless steel with this module. For engraving-only work on wood and leather, the 10W is enough.

standoutFeatures.title: One-pass cutting demos
standoutFeatures.body: Ortur demonstrates 10 mm plywood and 8 mm black acrylic in a single pass with this module.

standoutFeatures.title: Air pump included
standoutFeatures.body: The basic set ships with Ortur's Air Pump 1.0, which the company says cuts burn marks by about half.

standoutFeatures.title: Square spot for photos
